Project-modified Qt 6.12.0: CLDR 49 source provenance

CLDR common and exemplars data come from Unicode's official versioned
distribution. Their original Unicode License v3 texts are retained separately.
Exact source, generator, patch and generated-file hashes are recorded in
qt_cldr49_sources.json.

The 349 existing Qt language-code records are reused without modification.
They were compared with SIL Global's official 2026-10-15 ISO 639-3 registry
on 2026-11-14 and are byte-identical for this selected Qt language set.
Attribution: SIL Global, https://iso639-3.sil.org/ .
No complete ISO code table or its download archive is redistributed.

Regeneration uses the original Qt source records, the two redistributable
CLDR archives, two reviewed upstream compatibility patches, and one small
project generator option. It requires no full ISO registry input. The new
option preserves the original generator's default behavior and makes its
generated-source comment date reproducible.

The upstream Monrovia adaptation retains the existing minute-based metadata
representation of the historical 1972 transition at 00:45. It does not replace
OS time-zone offset data or claim second-precision metadata.
